already understand the risks. But when they will step away is another question, and we don't really know the answer yet
As 2026 unfolds, South Korea's stock market continues to experience intense volatility. On one side, foreign investors keep withdrawing capital. On
the other, individual investors continue buying with determination. People have very different views about where the market is heading. Some believe
that stocks are now undervalued and that the future still looks promising. Some are even continuing to borrow money to invest
convinced that the next rebound is just around the corner. And who knows? Maybe this time they'll be right. Of course
the optimistic scenario is entirely possible. South Korea is still home to some of the world's leading companies. It has a
powerful semiconductor industry, a role in AI, and strong potential drivers of long-term growth. If conditions develop favorably, the market could
absolutely resume its upward climb after this correction. But opportunity always comes with risk. Leverage remains extremely high. Household debt is
still among the highest in the world. Meanwhile, the real economy is recovering more slowly than many had hoped. When a
financial system is loaded with leverage, every shock becomes much more dangerous. It could be a change in global interest rates
a geopolitical crisis, an unexpected development in the semiconductor industry, or simply a sudden shift in market sentiment. Perhaps the most
important question to watch over the coming years is this: can South Korea find a way to help its younger generation
